routes.label: Square and add the two equations

question: Suppose that \(\sin a+\sin b=\sqrt{\tfrac53}\) and \(\cos a+\cos b=1.\) What is \(\cos(a-b)?\)
solution:
The identity
\[
\cos(a-b)=\cos a\cos b+\sin a\sin b
\]
shows which products we want. Squaring the given sums creates these products. Adding the squares also lets us use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) for each angle:
\[
\begin{aligned}
& (\sin a+\sin b)^2+(\cos a+\cos b)^2\\
&=2+2(\sin a\sin b+\cos a\cos b)\\
&=2+2\cos(a-b).
\end{aligned}
\]
From the given values, the same sum is \(5/3+1=8/3\). Therefore
\[
2+2\cos(a-b)=\frac83,
\qquad \cos(a-b)=\boxed{\frac13}.
\]
The answer is choice B.
